table.brief: Restaurant menu with section rows spanning all columns (Starters, Mains, Desserts): Dish / Description / Price / Allergens

understanding.purpose: Help diners choose dishes by comparing descriptions, prices and allergens within each course.
understanding.reading: Readers scan course headings and dish names, then read across each row for ingredients, price and allergens. Wrapped descriptions can create row height that also accommodates wrapped dish names or allergen lists.
groups: Dish and Description belong together as the name and explanation of each menu item.
Price and Allergens are compact decision aids read alongside each dish.
keep_intact: Individual dish-name and ingredient words where possible.
Each price as a single value.
Allergen names where possible, so they remain easy to identify.
may_wrap: Allergen lists between entries or words.

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Give the allergen column the width that kept the parenthesized name intact in r1B, taking one pixel from r1C's description column. This retains the compact dish and price widths while testing whether the better description wrapping survives.

preferred.name: r3C
preferred.note: Give allergens 2px more than r2A to test whether list entries group more naturally, while retaining enough width for the longest description word and all headers.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Move 6px from Description to Dish relative to r0A. Test whether improved dish-name grouping is worth narrower descriptions while retaining the intact allergen column.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Give dish names a little more room while preserving the successful allergen width. This explores whether better name wrapping is worth the narrower descriptions and any resulting row-height increase.

bad.name: r1C
bad.note: Move 1px from Allergens to Description relative to r0A. Test the boundary for preserving the allergen header and names while giving descriptions a little more room.
bad.why: The closing parenthesis in the dessert allergen is stranded on its own line.

bad.name: r2B
bad.note: Keep the allergen width that preserved the dessert entry and reclaim two pixels from Price for Description. Test whether the price header and values remain intact while longer descriptions gain breathing room.
bad.why: The Price header breaks within the word, weakening the column heading for a small gain in description width.

bad.name: r3A
bad.note: Give the description 1px more than r2A by taking it from allergens. This tests whether a small gain improves wrapping while keeping the price header and the longest dish and allergen words intact.
bad.why: The closing parenthesis in the dessert allergen is stranded on its own line.

bad.name: r3B
bad.note: Give the description more room by narrowing the dish column slightly. This tests whether better ingredient phrasing outweighs any additional wrapping of dish names.
bad.why: Croquettes splits off its final letter, and the dessert allergen has a stranded closing parenthesis.

rationale: r2A and r3C keep the dish names, prices, headers and allergen terms intact while giving the descriptions the largest share of the width. Their section bands clearly separate courses, and the row grid keeps each dish associated with its price and allergens despite substantial wrapping. Both have the same row heights and a similarly balanced distribution of space.

general: Protect row identifiers and critical labels from breaks within words.
Allocate width according to content and reading purpose; short numeric columns generally need less space than prose.
Judge wrapping in the context of complete rows and groups, not table height alone.
specific: Price needs 58 px here to keep its header intact.
The allergen column needs at least 91 px in these renders to keep the parenthesized hazelnut label together.
The two preferred allocations produce the same row heights despite moving 2 px between description and allergens.

tradeoffs: r2A gives descriptions a little more room; r3C gives allergens more breathing room. The shorter r1C and r3A save one line in the risotto row but strand punctuation in an allergen.
uncertain: The ranges describe the observed preferred endpoints, with the intervening allocation inferred rather than rendered. They are coordinated ranges: description and allergen widths must trade space within the 359 px total, not vary independently.

critique.good: All four headers and prices stay on one line. Dish names and allergen names remain intact, and the course bands give the long rows clear structure.
critique.problems: Descriptions form narrow, tall columns of short phrases, making the menu laborious to scan. Several dish names take three lines, though their wrapping does not usually add height beyond the descriptions.
critique.cause: The 112px description column leaves 91px for text. The 98px dish column is just wide enough for the longest unbreakable dish word, while the 91px allergen column preserves the allergen header and names.

critique.good: The wider dish column makes several names easier to read, particularly Roast Chicken Supreme. Prices remain compact and aligned.
critique.problems: The Allergens header breaks inside the word, as do Sulfites and hazelnut; the closing parenthesis in (wheat) is stranded on its own line. These breaks make safety information harder to scan, and the table is taller despite the wider dish column.
critique.cause: The 120px dish column takes space from the 71px allergen column, leaving only 50px for allergen text. The 110px description column remains narrow enough to control most row heights.

critique.good: The wider description column produces more natural phrases and reduces the height of some rows. Dish words and prices remain intact.
critique.problems: The Allergens header splits within the word, and hazelnut breaks across lines. The dessert allergen list becomes a tall stack and controls that row's height.
critique.cause: The 125px description column gains space at the expense of the 78px allergen column, which leaves only 57px for text.

critique.good: Course bands clearly separate the menu, prices stay intact, and dish names remain recognizable. The description column gives several phrases reasonable line lengths.
critique.problems: The Allergens header breaks across two lines, making the entire header disproportionately tall. In the dessert row, the closing parenthesis is stranded on its own line.
critique.cause: The 88px allergen column leaves too little text width for the header and the parenthesized allergen. The 98px dish column is already close to the minimum needed for its longest word.

critique.good: All four headers fit on one line, prices remain intact, and allergen names and parentheses stay together. Course headings and dish names are easy to find.
critique.problems: Descriptions become narrow, fragmented stacks, especially for the chicken and croquettes. This makes their rows tall and leaves substantial empty space in the neighboring cells.
critique.cause: The 106px description column has only 85px of text width. Allocating 104px to dishes and 91px to allergens preserves their words but leaves less room for the longest content.

critique.good: The single-line header and clear course bands establish a compact hierarchy. Compared with r1B, the wider description column improves phrasing and reduces several row heights while prices remain intact.
critique.problems: The dessert allergen ends with a lone closing parenthesis, and descriptions still form tall, narrow blocks. Dish names wrap frequently, though generally at natural boundaries.
critique.cause: The 90px allergen column fits its header but is just too narrow for the full parenthesized allergen. The 113px description column is constrained by the space needed for the other three columns.

critique.good: All headers and prices stay on one line. Course bands clearly divide the menu, and dish names and allergen terms remain intact.
critique.problems: Descriptions form narrow, tall stacks, leaving large empty areas in the price and allergen cells. The long rows make it harder to compare dishes across a course.
critique.cause: The 112px description column provides only 91px for text; several descriptions need seven or eight lines. The 58px price column is close to its practical minimum.

critique.good: The extra description width improves some phrases: the croquettes description keeps 'salt cod' together, and the risotto description takes one fewer line. Dish names and allergen terms remain intact.
critique.problems: The Price header breaks inside the word, making the header row taller and disrupting the otherwise clear column hierarchy. The description remains very narrow, and the saved line does not reduce the overall table height.
critique.cause: At 56px, the price column leaves only 35px for text, less than the header requires. Its 2px were transferred to the description column.

critique.good: All headers and prices remain intact, and the wider dish column preserves individual dish-name words. Course headings remain easy to find.
critique.problems: The wider dish column does not visibly improve the dish-name wrapping, while the chicken description gains a line and leaves 'jus' isolated. The table is consequently taller.
critique.cause: Moving 3px from the description to the dish column reduces description text width to 88px, triggering an extra line without a corresponding gain in the dish column.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r1C.why: Dish names and prices scan clearly, but the description wraps heavily and the dessert allergen ends with a stranded closing parenthesis.

r1B.why: Headers, dish names and allergens remain intact, but the narrow description column produces long, fragmented rows, including a stranded 'jus'.

r2A.why: The columns balance dish names, descriptions, prices and allergens well; words and headers remain intact, though descriptions still wrap heavily.

ref_equal.why: The description header and several dish names and ingredients break within words, while the price column has more space than it needs.

r2C.why: Headers and words stay intact, with clear dish and allergen columns; the description is narrow enough to leave 'jus' on its own line.

ref_auto.why: Dish names, prices and allergens remain legible, and the description has enough room for reasonably coherent phrases despite substantial wrapping.

raw.unsure: C and F are very close visually; both still require substantial wrapping in the description column.

ref_equal.why: Equal column widths waste space on prices while splitting the Description header, dish names, description words and allergen punctuation. The resulting tall rows are difficult to scan.

r1C.why: Headers and dish names remain intact, and descriptions have a little more room, but the dessert allergen ends with a stranded closing parenthesis.

r1B.why: Headers, dish names and allergen terms stay intact, including the dessert parenthesis. The narrower description column creates frequent wrapping and taller rows.

r2C.why: The columns preserve whole words and keep allergen details together; descriptions remain narrow but generally read in manageable phrases.

ref_auto.why: Dish names, prices and allergen details stay intact, with a compact price column leaving space for descriptions. The long descriptions still wrap frequently.

r2A.why: The price column is compact, dish names remain readable and the dessert allergen stays intact. Description lines are short, but the rows remain easy to associate.

raw.unsure: E and F are very close in their visible wrapping and proportions; the small difference between them has little apparent effect on reading.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
